name: Justinian I
description: Byzantine emperor whose jurists codified Roman law into the Corpus Juris Civilis — the foundation of most modern civil-law systems — while his generals briefly reconquered Italy and North Africa and his architects raised the Hagia Sophia.

name: Charlemagne
description: King of the Franks crowned Emperor of the Romans by Pope Leo III on Christmas Day 800, uniting most of western Europe for the first time since Rome. His court sparked the Carolingian Renaissance of learning, script, and administration.

name: Al-Khwarizmi
description: Persian polymath at Baghdad's House of Wisdom whose treatise on al-jabr gave algebra its name and whose Latinized name gave us 'algorithm'. His works transmitted Hindu-Arabic numerals to Europe.

name: William the Conqueror
description: Duke of Normandy who won the English crown at Hastings in 1066, replacing the Anglo-Saxon elite with Norman lords, commissioning the Domesday survey of his new kingdom, and permanently binding English institutions and language to continental Europe.

name: Saladin
description: Kurdish sultan of Egypt and Syria who united the Muslim Near East, crushed the crusader army at Hattin (1187), and retook Jerusalem — yet won a chivalrous reputation among his Frankish enemies during the Third Crusade against Richard the Lionheart.

name: Genghis Khan
description: Founder of the Mongol Empire, history's largest contiguous land empire. Unified the steppe tribes, revolutionized cavalry warfare and military organization, and opened Eurasia to unprecedented exchange — at catastrophic human cost to conquered populations.

name: Thomas Aquinas
description: Dominican friar whose Summa Theologiae synthesized Aristotelian philosophy with Christian doctrine, defining scholastic method and remaining the touchstone of Catholic theology. Canonized 1323.

name: Mansa Musa
description: Emperor of Mali whose 1324 hajj to Mecca, distributing so much gold that he depressed prices in Cairo for years, advertised West Africa's wealth to the world. He made Timbuktu a centre of Islamic scholarship.

name: Joan of Arc
description: Peasant visionary who convinced the Dauphin to give her an army, lifted the siege of Orléans, and turned the Hundred Years' War toward France before capture, an English-run heresy trial, and burning at nineteen. Rehabilitated 1456; canonized 1920.
